key_insight: A deep learning CTA vessel-segmentation model was very accurate technically, but it did not improve vertebral artery dissection detection in a reader study.
clinical_relevance: The tool may help visualize vascular anatomy, but its current form should not be assumed to improve real-world diagnosis of vertebral artery dissection.
method: Trained nnU-Net v2 on 101 manually segmented CTA studies with 5-fold cross-validation.
Externally tested on 40 CTA cases, including 22 with vertebral artery dissection.
Ran a 10-reader crossover study comparing CTA interpretation with vs without segmentation-based augmentation.
evidence_signal: Segmentation performance was strong (Dice 0.96 ± 0.01), but diagnostic accuracy was worse with augmentation than without (0.72 vs 0.84, P < .001).
watch_item: High segmentation accuracy did not translate into better diagnostic performance, so workflow integration and clinical validation remain major concerns.
paper_title: Does Deep Learning Vascular Segmentation on CTA Improve Vertebral Artery Dissection Detection?
